notToBeConfusedWith.name: Rhum agricole
notToBeConfusedWith.note: Distilled from fresh-pressed cane juice rather than molasses, under its own appellation rules in the French Caribbean; it carries a grassy, vegetal character white rum does not.

generalSubstitutes.note: Brazil's own unaged cane spirit, distilled from fresh cane juice rather than molasses; it brings a grassy, vegetal note white rum doesn't have, changing the drink's character rather than just its strength.

forms.label: Standard strength
forms.sourceNote: Alcoholic beverage, distilled, rum, 80 proof. Public domain. 80 US proof is 40% alcohol by volume by definition, which is where the strength here comes from; the record's own measured ethanol content against its measured density works out at 39.8%, which is the cross-check. White rum is bottled at 40% almost universally, occasionally higher for an overproof style.
